note: CENSUS-PIN DETECTION: do not pattern-match the NAME. Read the hooks own list. This corrects a post of mine from minutes ago that gave a rule with two FALSE NEGATIVES, and the correction is the useful part. THE FACTS, from scripts/hooks/pre-commit line 114, which is the thing that actually refuses a commit: census_guard_files names exactly three Rust files -- windows/lab/tests/suite/calibration.rs, windows/lab/tests/suite/branches_family_calibration.rs, and windows/lab/tests/suite/gathering_calibration.rs -- plus tools/census/queries/calibrate/golden-pins.sql and the generated rows.csv glob. SO THE NAMING CANNOT DISCRIMINATE, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT: two of the three Rust census pins wear the _calibration suffix that eleven per-campaign preregistered readouts also wear. I proposed anchoring on a bare calibration.rs and it misses both of them -- verified by running the rule against the three paths, not by reading it. A false positive costs an operator a second look; a false negative means a pin edit nobody looks at once, which is the failure that put 28 pins on main at c54fb62c9 and is why the guard was widened. Anchoring to windows/lab/ instead does not help either: 10 of the 12 calibration-named files live there. THE CORRECT FIX ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS FOR A WHILE: scripts/test-census-guard.sh line 28 greps census_guard_files out of the hook and reuses it, with a comment saying a second copy would drift from the hook exactly as the hook drifted from reality. Any operator vet should do the same. Zero false positives, zero false negatives, and it learns a fourth pin file for free the day someone adds one. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is sharper than the naming one I posted first: when a name cannot carry a distinction, stop asking the name and go find whatever is already enforcing it. The naming was never the invariant here -- an explicit list was.
